clue.text: Rock climber — girl with youth leader in gym

indicators.note: the youth's leading letter is placed inside the girl's name

parts.note: Barbara is a girl's name

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of youth

parts.note: PE, physical education, is school gym

explanation.surface: A girl climbs with the head of a youth group in the gym.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock' is the Rock of Gibraltar, home of the wild Barbary macaques, so the climber is an animal, not a mountaineer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Barbary macaques living wild on Gibraltar famously scramble about the Rock, so they are its climbers.

clue.text: Boatman's first on boat, the so-and-so

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece placed on top of another comes before it
the first letter of Boatman's is taken alone

parts.note: a lighter is a flat-bottomed barge for loading ships

explanation.surface: The bargeman stands on his boat, the rotter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a down-clue charade signal: B sits on top of LIGHTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A blighter is British slang for an annoying person, a euphemistic insult like so-and-so.

clue.text: Grown-up girl having two other halves?

definitions.note: a phrase describing a state, matching the noun for that state

parts.note: big means grown-up, as in 'when you're big'
Amy is a girl's name

explanation.surface: An adult woman with two partners at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Other half' is a jokey term for a spouse; two of them at once is the offence.
explanation.definitionFit: Bigamy is being married to two spouses at once, and a spouse is jokingly one's other half.

clue.text: Police officer is engaged

definitions.meaning: old British slang for a detective or policeman
occupied, as a phone line or a person is

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both underworld slang for a detective and an ordinary word for occupied or tied up.

clue.text: Live bats seek fast food

parts.note: to be is to live or exist

indicators.note: bats means crazy, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Bats that are alive go hunting for a quick meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bats' looks like the animals but is the anagram signal on SEEK FAST; 'fast food' tempts as the definition, yet 'fast' is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Beefsteaks are slices of beef for grilling, a kind of food.

clue.text: Animals trained by Arabs etc

indicators.note: trained means schooled into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Creatures being schooled by Arab handlers and so on.
explanation.definitionFit: Bearcats are mammals, either the binturong of Asia or the red panda, so animals.

clue.text: Cycling's no good — I dress for the beach

indicators.note: no means without, so the letter for good is removed

parts.note: biking is cycling; the 's is 'is', a link

explanation.surface: Cycling is no good, says someone, I'll put on swimwear instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A bikini is a two-piece swimsuit, an outfit worn on the beach.

clue.text: Hammer and nails initially kept in sack

indicators.note: one letter is held inside the word for sack

parts.note: a bag is a sack

indicators.note: the first letter of nails is taken

explanation.surface: A hammer and nails are stored in a sack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hammer' looks like a noun but is the verb: bang is to strike hard.
explanation.definitionFit: To bang is to hit or strike loudly, as one does when hammering.

clue.text: No doubles for PM? 1 certainly, not 4

indicators.note: each doubled letter in the Prime Minister's name loses one copy

parts.note: Clement Attlee was a British Prime Minister
the numeral one is I
sure means certainly

explanation.surface: No twin stays for the Prime Minister, one assumes, not occupied.
explanation.walkthrough: '4' cross-refers to the answer to 4 Down (BUSY); its opposite is the definition. Attlee was Labour Prime Minister 1945-51.
explanation.definitionFit: Being at leisure means having free time, the opposite of being busy, the answer to 4 Down.

clue.text: Musical life in Rome following emperor's lead

indicators.note: the Latin word comes after the emperor's first letter
the leading letter of emperor's is taken

parts.note: vita is Latin, the language of Rome, for life

explanation.surface: A show about Roman life after the emperor led.
explanation.definitionFit: Evita is the Lloyd Webber and Rice stage musical about Eva Perón.

clue.text: Vagrant happy to occupy niche

indicators.note: one word moves into and fills the other

parts.note: a bay is a recess or alcove, like a niche
glad means happy

explanation.surface: A tramp is pleased to settle in an alcove.
explanation.definitionFit: A bag lady is a homeless woman carrying her possessions in bags, a vagrant.

clue.text: Divergent royalist?

definitions.meaning: splitting into branches, as a road does
read as two words, on the side of the monarch

explanation.definitionFit: Forking means dividing into branches, so divergent; split as 'for king' it describes a supporter of the crown.

clue.text: Irritable swimmer keeps refusing alcohol

indicators.note: one word holds the other inside it

parts.note: a ray is a flat fish, a swimmer
TT means teetotal

explanation.surface: A grumpy swimmer still won't take a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratty is British informal for bad-tempered or cross.

clue.text: One wearing black, a little New Yorker

parts.note: a goth dresses in black clothing
a mite is a little thing or bit

explanation.surface: A small New Yorker dressed in black.
explanation.walkthrough: Gotham is a nickname for New York City.
explanation.definitionFit: A Gothamite is an inhabitant of Gotham, the nickname for New York City.

clue.text: Buddy Polanski's style of wrestling

parts.note: Buddy Greco was an American jazz singer
Roman Polanski is the film director

explanation.surface: A friend of Polanski's preferred grappling style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buddy' looks like 'friend' but is the singer's first name, as Polanski's first name is the second piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Greco-Roman is a style of wrestling banning holds below the waist.

clue.text: Dean's heart softened, somehow, in film

indicators.note: the heart of Dean is its middle letters
somehow means in some unknown way, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: James Dean grew tender, somehow, in a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart' gives EA from Dean, which joins SOFTENED for the anagram; Dean starred in the film.
explanation.definitionFit: East of Eden is the 1955 film from Steinbeck's novel, starring James Dean.

clue.text: High-flyers, when transported, have similar cars

indicators.note: transported means carried away, so the letters are moved into new order

explanation.surface: Executives on the move own matching cars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High-flyers' suggests successful people; here they are senior RAF officers.
explanation.definitionFit: Air vice-marshals are senior officers of the Royal Air Force, so literally high in rank and fliers.

clue.text: An idiot struggling to grasp egghead's mental power

indicators.note: the jumbled letters hold another inside
struggling suggests things in disorder, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: the head of egg is its first letter, E

explanation.surface: A fool strains to understand an intellectual's brainpower.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideation is the capacity for forming ideas, a mental faculty.

clue.text: Something consuming resources in Jersey, possibly an environmental problem

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a drain on resources uses them up
Jersey is one of the Channel Islands, CI

explanation.surface: Something eating into Jersey's assets may be an ecological worry.
explanation.walkthrough: Jersey is a British island off the French coast; 'Something consuming resources' reads as a single phrase, a drain on them.
explanation.definitionFit: Acid rain is precipitation polluted by emissions, a well-known ecological hazard.

clue.text: Privately composing tunes to entertain US city

indicators.note: entertaining means taking in a guest, so one word holds another
composing means arranging, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: Reno is a city in Nevada

explanation.surface: Quietly writing music to amuse an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composing' scrambles the tunes into ENTUS, and the city goes in after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Entre nous is a French phrase meaning between ourselves, so in confidence.

clue.text: Italian workers' examination

parts.note: TU, a trade union, is a body of workers
a scan is a close examination

explanation.surface: Labourers undergo a check-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuscan means from Tuscany, a region of Italy, so Italian.

clue.text: Letter from Greece about favoured animals

definitions.note: plural, as the word can be used as its own plural

indicators.note: one word goes around the other

parts.note: rho is a letter of the Greek alphabet
in means in favour, popular

explanation.surface: A Greek note mentions favourite beasts.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhino is short for rhinoceros and can be its own plural, so animals.

clue.text: Admit defeat when rule is broken by bridge player

indicators.note: a letter breaks into the word for rule

parts.note: to reign is to rule
South is one of the four bridge positions, S

explanation.surface: Give up when a card-player breaks the rules.
explanation.definitionFit: To resign is to give up, conceding the game.

clue.text: Chap retreating to useless house in African kingdom

parts.note: Les is a man's name

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards
read as 'use-less', the letters of use are dropped

parts.note: the word as written before its letters are removed

explanation.surface: A man withdraws to an unusable house in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreating' turns TO to OT, and 'useless' strips USE from HOUSE, leaving HO.
explanation.definitionFit: Lesotho is a mountainous kingdom wholly surrounded by South Africa.

clue.text: Borders of Lincoln green? Right!

indicators.note: the borders of the phrase are its opening and closing letter pairs

explanation.surface: Is Lincoln's rim green? Correct!
explanation.walkthrough: The first two letters and last two of 'Lincoln green' are taken. Lincoln green is the cloth colour of Robin Hood.
explanation.definitionFit: A lien is a legal right to hold property until a debt is paid.

clue.text: Clock, say

definitions.meaning: clock is slang for notice or watch

explanation.definitionFit: Observe means both notice or see, slang 'clock', and to remark or comment.

clue.text: Beast appearing in county briefly

parts.note: an ox is a beast of burden
on means appearing, as a show is on

explanation.surface: A bull appears in a shire, in short.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxon is the abbreviation for Oxfordshire, an English county.

clue.text: Source of inspiration kept in refrigerator

indicators.note: the answer is held within the word that follows

explanation.surface: Inspiration is stored in the fridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato is the Muse of lyric poetry, a muse being a source of inspiration.

clue.text: Next to remark in an undertone about hunger

indicators.note: one word goes around the other

parts.note: an aside is a quiet remark
to long is to hunger for

explanation.surface: Beside him came a whispered comment on hunger.
explanation.definitionFit: Alongside means beside or next to.
